newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end down, first half gloom remains.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end down, first half gloom remains.

text.p: ** Bombay shares end lower on Thursday as mood stays gloomy on onslaught of disappointing first half results
** Shares of Tata Chemicals hit after first half net falls below last year; Tata Tea ends lower as results fail to cheer
** The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) finishes 22.12 points lower at provisional 3040.38
** April-September industrial growth slows to 4.8 percent from 12.8 percent during the corresponding period last year
** Finance firm IDBI reports modest 2.0 percent growth in net for the six months to September 30, 1996
Bombay shares closed lower on Thursday as disappointing first half results continued to pour in and traders said many unpleasant surprises were still in store.
"Basically there was quite a bit of selling in pivotals probably due to the bad results and the news that industrial production figures are down," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
India's April-September industrial growth has slowed to 4.8 percent from 12.8 percent during the corresponding period last year, according to the latest data released on Wednesday.
"Investors are waiting for some positive signal," the trader said.

Shares of Tata Chemicals -- which said late on Wednesday its net profit during the six months to September 30, 1996 fell to 1,319.9 million rupees from 1,751.5 million a year ago -- were badly hit by the announcment.
The share plunged 19.50 rupees or 9.75 percent to 180.50 on the Bombay bourse.
Finance firm IDBI's results fell below market expectations when it announced a modest 2.0 percent rise in its net profit for the first half of 1996/97 (April-March).
Analysts said the worst was yet to come.

"Despite many downward estimate revisions earlier in the year, analysts and the market may be disappointed with half-year earnings that will be announced in the current reporting season," Rupa Bose, regional analyst and India strategist at Paribas Capital Markets in Singapore, said in a note to investors.
Bose said the market had underestimated the impact of tight money and infrastructure problems with power and rail transport faced by Indian companies in late 1995.

Shares of Tata Tea were not cheered by a 25 percent jump in first half net. The firm said the year-ago figure was adjusted for impact of increased wages in Kerala. It said profit margins in the second half would be hit on the back of falling tea prices.
